moat_against: Customer concentration: US DoD/Navy and a few primes set budgets, timing and terms
Program/budget risk: ground defense sales -8% in Q2 2026, Defense Electronics shipment timing slips
No network effects — moat is qualification/engineering depth, erodible by competitors and in-housing primes
Commercial nuclear/SMR upside is slow and policy-dependent
CEO transition in January adds execution uncertainty
moat_for: Sole-source/qualified status on naval nuclear propulsion and reactor coolant pumps — slow, safety-critical requalification
Embedded content on long-life platforms (submarines, carriers, F-35) = decades of spares, upgrades, service
Defense Electronics margins in the high-20s — proven pricing power in mission computing
$4.5B backlog, up 10% since Dec 2025, 1.16x book-to-bill — multi-year visibility
Diversified across naval, defense electronics, commercial aero and nuclear — no single program decides it
moat_justification: Qualified, often sole-source positions on naval nuclear propulsion, reactor coolant pumps and flight/mission-critical electronics on platforms that run for decades, with aftermarket and spares annuity and high-20s Defense Electronics margins; bounded by US government/prime customer concentration, program/budget timing risk, no network effects, and slow policy-dependent commercial nuclear upside.
name: Curtiss-Wright Corporation
one_liner: High-quality defense/nuclear compounder, moat 7/10 — but at $501.49 it does not clear 15% in any scenario (weighted IRR 8.85%, IV@15 $231.48); it would need to fall to ~$231 to clear the hurdle on the weighted case.
